reviewer: Codex /root; same-context mathematical self-review, not independent human or theorem review
conditional_scope: Formula/specification review only; no empirical assumption, originality, GPU interface or efficacy verified.

formal_object.rationale: A smooth legal trajectory Y(t), small phase offsets tau in a fixed endpoint-preserving basis, amplitude basis B; desired model/input-derived residual r; P is the phase Jacobian. The stated object/domain, rather than the official unsquared Chamfer, is the object of this conditional derivation.

operations_and_conditions.rationale: C05: Y(t+tau)=Y(t)+Ydot(t) tau+O(tau^2) -> First-order phase direction; condition: Smooth trajectory and small monotone time warp; F06: Weighted least squares in phase and amplitude blocks -> Profiled amplitude equation; condition: Unconstrained phase elimination only when no phase inequality is active; H02: Overlap of phase and amplitude spans -> Separate identifiable amplitude from timing; condition: Jacobian rank and gauge are checked All current edges remain conditional where model/data availability is not established.

derivation.rationale: Weighted phase elimination gives the Schur projection M and the positive-ridge amplitude solve; a full unconstrained block solve agrees. The formula is invalid when time monotonicity constraints are active. Overlapping phase/amplitude spans are unidentifiable and a second-order remainder remains. Native reference timestamps stay fixed.

assumptions.rationale: Conditional validity requires: Time warp is internal to the method; output is still evaluated at every original benchmark timestamp, with untouched references.; Phase targets use legal input/model evidence and no confirmation labels.; Endpoints, monotonicity, derivative regularity and interpolation error are checked; positive amplitude ridge lambda>0 ensures the profiled inverse is defined.; Input evidence may not distinguish timing from amplitude; then this is an identifiability boundary rather than a successful repair. These are obligations, not observations about ActionBench.

method_expression.rationale: Jointly infer a small anchored monotone phase correction and amplitude correction; use the profiled formula only in the unconstrained phase regime; render outputs at original times. The reviewed construction is Endpoint-preserving monotone phase/amplitude block inference.. This is a specification, not an implemented method.

prediction_and_falsifier.rationale: The construction predicts: Timing-dominated errors should respond to phase correction while amplitude-only shrinkage loses motion; amplitude-dominated errors should show the opposite pattern. It can be rejected by: Reject if ordinary lag/alignment with equal evidence/budget is sufficient, or phase/amplitude remains unidentifiable on the native task. This contrast is specified before any new-method experiment.

closest_alternative.rationale: Named alternatives: Classical phase-amplitude registration and Schur projection; simple lag correction, smoothing and displacement scaling. Claimed operational difference: Separates two competing mechanisms instead of interpreting every motion mismatch as coordinate noise; classical registration remains prior art. This check verifies an explicit comparator and conditional delta, not completed novelty clearance.
